briefdescription.para: Initialize (or reset) a protothread so it starts from the top.
Open a protothread body. Must be the first statement in the protothread function, before any PT_* operations.

detaileddescription.para: Expands to the head of a switch statement that jumps to the last saved continuation point.

briefdescription.para: Close a protothread body. Returns PT_ENDED and resets the continuation so the thread can be restarted if desired.

memberdef.name: PT_WAIT_UNTIL
memberdef.initializer: do { \ (pt)->lc = __LINE__; \ SYN_FALLTHROUGH; /* intentional Duff's device */ \ case __LINE__: \ if (!(cond)) { \ return PT_IDLE; \ } \ } while (0)

briefdescription.para: Block until cond evaluates to true.

detaileddescription.para: Each time the protothread is polled and cond is false, it returns PT_IDLE and resumes at this point on the next call.

briefdescription.para: Block while cond is true. Dual of PT_WAIT_UNTIL.

memberdef.name: PT_PASS
memberdef.initializer: do { \ _pt_yield_flag = 0; \ (pt)->lc = __LINE__; \ SYN_FALLTHROUGH; \ case __LINE__: \ if (_pt_yield_flag == 0) { \ return PT_IDLE; \ } \ } while (0)

briefdescription.para: Pass the remainder of this scheduler round with PT_IDLE.

detaileddescription.para: Signals that the protothread has no immediate work right now so other ready tasks (including lower priorities) can run this round.

memberdef.name: PT_CONTINUE
memberdef.initializer: do { \ _pt_yield_flag = 0; \ (pt)->lc = __LINE__; \ SYN_FALLTHROUGH; \ case __LINE__: \ if (_pt_yield_flag == 0) { \ return PT_MORE; \ } \ } while (0)

briefdescription.para: Yield after completing a work chunk with PT_MORE.

detaileddescription.para: Signals that the protothread actively has more work remaining and should remain in the scheduler's Work tier.

briefdescription.para: Abort the protothread immediately and return PT_EXITED.
Reset the protothread and restart from PT_BEGIN on next call.

memberdef.name: PT_SPAWN
memberdef.initializer: do { \ PT_INIT(child); \ (pt)->lc = __LINE__; \ SYN_FALLTHROUGH; \ case __LINE__: { \ SYN_PT_Status _pt_child_st = (func); \ if (_pt_child_st < PT_EXITED) { \ return _pt_child_st; \ } \ } \ } while (0)

briefdescription.para: Spawn a child protothread and block until it exits.

detaileddescription.para: Propagates the child's PT_IDLE or PT_MORE status verbatim while running.

pt
Parent protothread.
child
Child protothread (SYN_PT struct).
func
Expression that calls the child's function, e.g. child_func(&child_pt).
The func expression is evaluated on EVERY scheduler poll until the child exits. Never pass expressions with side-effects (e.g. counter++, function calls that modify state). Pre-evaluate arguments before calling PT_SPAWN.
Usage: staticSYN_PTchild_pt; PT_SPAWN(pt,&child_pt,child_func(&child_pt));

memberdef.name: PT_DELAY_MS

briefdescription.para: Non-blocking delay for ms milliseconds.

detaileddescription.para: Requires a uint32_t variable to store the deadline. When used with the scheduler, pass &(task)->delay_until. For standalone use, pass any persistent uint32_t *.

simplesect.para: The target is reset to 0 (the scheduler's "no deadline pending" sentinel) once the delay completes. A deadline left in place would read as "in the future" again after the tick counter advances 2^31 ms (~24.8 days) past it, freezing the task. A computed deadline of exactly 0 (tick wrap) is nudged to 1 (or 0xFFFFFFFF when clamped == INT32_MAX) so it cannot alias the sentinel while keeping (int32_t)(dl - now) > 0. Durations exceeding INT32_MAX ms are clamped to INT32_MAX ms, and ms is evaluated exactly once.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to a uint32_t that will hold the deadline tick.

briefdescription.para: Convenience form for use with the scheduler's SYN_Task (milliseconds).
Non-blocking sub-millisecond delay for us microseconds.

detaileddescription.para: Requires a user-supplied persistent uint32_t variable (e.g., static uint32_t us_target;). Does not modify SYN_Task.delay_until to avoid corrupting the millisecond scheduler timebase.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to a uint32_t variable holding the microsecond deadline.

memberdef.name: PT_BLOCK_EVENT

briefdescription.para: Block until ANY bit in mask is set in the event group.

detaileddescription.para: Unlike PT_WAIT_EVENT (which polls every scheduler pass), this macro sets the task state to BLOCKED. The scheduler skips the task entirely until the event fires, saving CPU and enabling proper tickless sleep.
Matched flags are atomically captured and auto-cleared when the scheduler dispatches the woken task.

parameterdescription.para: Bitmask of event flags to wait for (any of them).

memberdef.name: PT_BLOCK_EVENT_WITH_TIMEOUT
memberdef.initializer: do { \ uint32_t *_syn_ef_out = (out_flags); \ if (syn_task_arm_event_wait((task), (SYN_EventFlags *)(grp), (mask), true, \ (uint32_t)(timeout_ms), _syn_ef_out)) { \ while ((task)->wait_event != NULL) { \ syn_task_park_blocked((task)); \ PT_PASS(pt); \ } \ (task)->delay_until = 0U; \ { \ uint32_t *_syn_ef_post = (out_flags); \ if (_syn_ef_post != NULL) { \ *_syn_ef_post = (task)->wait_mask; \ } \ } \ (task)->wait_mask = 0U; \ } \ } while (0)

briefdescription.para: Block task execution (SYN_TASK_BLOCKED) until ANY bit in mask is set OR timeout_ms milliseconds elapse.

detaileddescription.para: Combines event-flag blocking with millisecond deadline tracking. The task is skipped by the scheduler until either the event fires or the timeout deadline passes.
Matched event flags are captured into out_flags (if non-NULL) and auto-cleared ONLY if the event actually fired before the timeout. Check *out_flags != 0 to determine if the event fired vs timed out.

parameterdescription.para: Bitmask of event flags to wait for.
Pointer to uint32_t receiving matched flags (or 0 on timeout).

memberdef.name: PT_BLOCK_CONDITION
memberdef.initializer: do { \ while (1) { \ syn_port_enter_critical(); \ if ((task)->state == (uint8_t)SYN_TASK_READY) { \ (task)->state = (uint8_t)SYN_TASK_BLOCKED; \ SYN_PT_STATE_BARRIER(); \ } \ syn_port_exit_critical(); \ if (cond) { \ syn_port_enter_critical(); \ if ((task)->state == (uint8_t)SYN_TASK_BLOCKED) { \ (task)->state = (uint8_t)SYN_TASK_READY; \ } \ syn_port_exit_critical(); \ break; \ } \ PT_PASS(pt); \ } \ } while (0)

briefdescription.para: Sleep task (SYN_TASK_BLOCKED) until explicitly resumed.

detaileddescription.para:
This macro does NOT poll cond on each scheduler tick. Once the task yields as BLOCKED, the scheduler skips it entirely. The condition is only re-evaluated when the task is explicitly woken by an ISR or driver calling syn_task_resume(task).
For polled condition blocking, use PT_WAIT_UNTIL(pt, cond) instead. For event-flag-driven blocking, use PT_BLOCK_EVENT(pt, task, grp, mask).

briefdescription.para: Protothreads — stackless cooperative coroutines for C.

detaileddescription.para: Protothreads provide lightweight, cooperative multitasking without requiring a separate stack per thread. Each protothread is a normal C function that uses macros to save and restore its execution position via the switch/__LINE__ continuation trick (Duff's device).
A protothread costs 2 bytes of RAM (the continuation variable).

listitem.para: You cannot use a bare switch statement inside a protothread body (use if/else if chains instead).
Local variables are NOT preserved across yield/wait points. Store persistent state in static variables, globals, or a struct passed via the task's user_data pointer.
A protothread must reside entirely within a single function.
